# Code Review Report

## Review Summary

This branch is tightly scoped around changing `scene-writer` to return compact savepoint references by default and documenting the new `includeContent` opt-in. The Python implementation, wrapper update, and unit coverage all look coherent, but the companion-file sweep is incomplete: one changed agent workflow now contains an internal contract contradiction, two downstream agents still assume `revise` returns full prose, and the live gotcha note still documents the old assemble-chapter savepoint behavior.

**Files Reviewed:** 5
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 4 Warning, 0 Suggestion

## Findings

### Warning Findings

[W-01] `chapter-writer` still promises full chapter text after switching `assemble-chapter` to compact refs
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/chapter-writer.md
Lines: 37-39
Description: Step 6 now correctly states that `scene-writer assemble-chapter` returns only `{chapter_ref, char_count, scene_count}` and writes the prose to `chapter_{N}/chapter_content`. Step 8 immediately after that still instructs the subagent to "Return the assembled chapter" to the orchestrator, but there is no intervening `savepoint-mgr load` or `includeContent: true` instruction. The orchestrator's downstream phases consume chapter text, so this leaves the runtime workflow internally inconsistent: the subagent no longer has the chapter prose in-hand by the documented steps.
Suggestion: Either call `assemble-chapter` with `includeContent: true` when the subagent must return prose immediately, or add an explicit load step from `chapter_{N}/chapter_content` before returning. Update Step 8 wording to match the actual payload.

[W-02] `final-editor` still assumes `scene-writer revise` returns revised prose inline
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/final-editor.md
Lines: 45-48
Description: Both revise loops instruct the agent to call `scene-writer` with `operation: "revise"` and then "replace the in-memory chapter text with the returned text." After this branch, `revise` now returns a compact payload by default (`scene_ref`, `savepoint_step`, `char_count`) unless `includeContent: true` is passed. As written, the next time `final-editor` runs it will read a response shape that no longer contains the text it is told to thread forward.
Suggestion: Update each `revise` call site to either pass `includeContent: true` or reload the prose from the returned savepoint reference before mutating in-memory chapter text.

[W-03] `prose-scrubber` still assumes `scene-writer revise` returns revised prose inline
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/prose-scrubber.md
Lines: 44
Description: Step 5 tells the agent to call `scene-writer revise` repeatedly and, after each success, "replace the in-memory chapter text with the returned text." That no longer matches the tool contract introduced by this branch: default `revise` responses are compact references, not prose bodies. This is exactly the sort of companion-agent drift the review checklist calls out for interface changes in `.opencode/tools/` and agent docs.
Suggestion: Mirror the new contract here as well: either pass `includeContent: true` on each `revise` call or load the content from the returned `scene_ref` / `savepoint_step` before continuing the loop.

[W-04] Live gotcha note still documents the old assemble-chapter savepoint behavior
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: .github/notes/gotchas.md
Lines: 84-99
Description: Gotcha #005 still says `scene-writer assemble-chapter` "does not create a savepoint" and requires an explicit `savepoint-mgr save`. This branch changes the implementation and docs to auto-save assembled output to `chapter_{N}/chapter_content`. `gotchas.md` is a live knowledge source, not historical audit output, so leaving it stale will actively mislead agents and humans who consult the notes before planning or debugging.
Suggestion: Rewrite Gotcha #005 to describe the new behavior (`chapter_{N}/chapter_content` is written automatically), remove the obsolete manual-save guidance, and reindex the corresponding ChromaDB entry after the Markdown source is updated.

## Overall Assessment

The code changes in the touched implementation files are close to merge-ready, but the branch is not fully reviewed-clean yet because the interface change was not carried through the companion instruction and knowledge files that rely on `scene-writer` return shapes. The main risk is runtime workflow drift: agents that still expect inline prose will mis-handle successful `revise` calls, and the stale gotcha note will teach the opposite of the new `assemble-chapter` behavior. Fix the companion docs and agent instructions in the same PR so the tool contract is consistent across code, tests, and operational guidance.
